title: Dip and Dip Direction from Normal Vector
equation: Dip = arccos(nz);  Dip Direction = atan2(nx, ny)  (adjusted to 0–360°)

nz.description: Vertical component of unit normal vector (positive upward)

nx.description: Easting component of unit normal vector

ny.description: Northing component of unit normal vector

applicability: Normal vector must point upward (nz > 0); if not, reverse sign. Convention: dip direction = azimuth that the plane dips toward (downhill direction of steepest descent). Ensure coordinate system is georeferenced (survey-registered point cloud).

title: Planarity Index from Eigenvalues

λ₁.description: Largest eigenvalue of local covariance matrix

applicability: Computed from k-nearest neighbors around each point. Additional shape descriptors: linearity L = (λ₁-λ₂)/λ₁; scattering S = λ₃/λ₁. Filter for P > 0.3–0.5 to isolate planar surfaces before discontinuity extraction.

title: Terzaghi Orientation Bias Correction
equation: w = 1 / cos(δ)  where δ = arccos(|n_disc · n_face|)

w.description: Weight applied to each discontinuity for unbiased frequency estimation

δ.description: Angle between discontinuity normal and face/sampling normal

n_face.description: Unit normal of the rock face (or line of sight direction)

applicability: Cap weight at δ_max ≈ 70–80° (w_max ≈ 3–6) to avoid instability for near-parallel features. Discontinuities with δ > 80° are in the blind zone and cannot be reliably detected from that viewing direction. Requires multi-view scanning to cover all orientations.

title: True Spacing from Plane Equations
equation: d = |D₂ - D₁|  for parallel planes a×x + b×y + c×z = D

d.description: True (perpendicular) spacing between two parallel discontinuities

D₁, D₂.description: Plane constants (a,b,c are the same unit normal for parallel planes)

applicability: For non-parallel planes within a joint set, project planes onto the mean set normal direction. Spacing = distance between successive intercepts along a virtual scanline perpendicular to the mean plane. True spacing eliminates the apparent-to-true correction needed in manual scanline surveys.

title: RQD from Discontinuity Frequency

RQD.description: Rock Quality Designation estimated from frequency

λ.description: Mean discontinuity frequency per meter (all sets combined) = 1/mean spacing

applicability: Priest & Hudson (1976) theoretical relationship assuming negative exponential spacing distribution. Equivalent to percentage of 0.1 m or longer intact lengths. Allows estimation of RQD from remotely-measured spacing without core recovery.

title: Z₂ Roughness Parameter from Profile

Z₂.description: Root mean square of first derivative of profile (roughness parameter)

yi.description: Profile elevation at sample point i

xi.description: Profile distance at sample point i

applicability: Correlates to JRC: JRC = 32.2 + 32.47 × log₁₀(Z₂) (Tse & Cruden 1979, 0.5 mm interval). Resolution-dependent — use consistent sampling interval. Extract profiles from point cloud along discontinuity surface. Minimum profile length 100 mm; ISRM recommends characterizing at multiple scales.

title: Fisher Distribution — Mean Orientation and Dispersion

R.description: Resultant length of summed unit normal vectors

nᵢ.description: Unit normal vector for each discontinuity

applicability: Fisher distribution is the spherical equivalent of the normal distribution. Mean orientation = direction of resultant vector R. κ > 100: very tight cluster (well-defined joint set). κ < 10: highly dispersed. Cone of confidence (α₉₅) for the mean: cos(α₉₅) = 1 - (N-R)/R × [(1/p)^(1/(N-1)) - 1] where p = 0.05.

title: Minimum Detectable Discontinuity Size
equation: L_min ≈ k × s  where s = point spacing on the face

L_min.description: Minimum discontinuity trace length that can be reliably detected

k.description: Multiplier (typically 5–10 points needed to fit a plane)

s.description: Mean point spacing on the rock face at scanning distance

applicability: At 50 m range with typical TLS (5 mm point spacing): L_min ≈ 25–50 mm. At 200 m range (20 mm spacing): L_min ≈ 100–200 mm. UAS photogrammetry at 30 m flight altitude: ~15–30 mm GSD → L_min ≈ 75–300 mm. Detection sensitivity depends on both point density and discontinuity aperture/contrast.

title: Angular Accuracy of Extracted Orientations

σ_θ.description: Angular uncertainty in extracted dip/dip direction

N_facet.description: Number of points in the segmented facet

applicability: Typical TLS: σ_pos ≈ 3–5 mm at 50 m range. For a facet with 100 points: σ_θ ≈ 1–3°. Comparable to compass/clinometer accuracy (±2–5°). Large facets (many points) yield more accurate orientations. Registration and georeferencing errors add systematic bias.

title: Block Volume from Joint Sets (Palmström)
equation: Vb = (s₁ × s₂ × s₃) / (sin γ₁₂ × sin γ₁₃ × sin γ₂₃)

s₁, s₂, s₃.description: Mean true spacings of three dominant joint sets

applicability: Used in GSI estimation and rockfall volume assessment. For 3 orthogonal sets: Vb = s₁×s₂×s₃. Random jointing with frequency λ: Vb ≈ β/λ³ where β depends on randomness (β = 27 for 3 orthogonal sets, β = 36 for random). Remote sensing provides s and γ for all visible sets simultaneously.
